what_this_proves: That two implementations turn the same authorization into the same bytes, and therefore the same hash. A one-character disagreement here means nothing either party signs will ever verify against the other, and it is invisible until two implementations meet.
rules: UTF-8. One "key=value" record per line, joined with LF (0x0A). No trailing newline.
Keys appear in the order given by the profile's boundsSchema.keyOrder / scopeSchema.keyOrder — NOT alphabetical order.
An optional key with no value is omitted entirely (no record). A key present with an empty string renders as "key=". Never a placeholder.
Every required key is included explicitly.
Numbers use the shortest round-trippable form: 20.0 serializes as "20".
A value MUST NOT contain a raw LF or CR. Such input is refused (BOUNDS_INVALID_VALUE / SCOPE_INVALID_VALUE) — never silently stripped or encoded.
Any other byte that is "=" (0x3D), "%" (0x25), or outside printable ASCII 0x20-0x7E is percent-encoded (RFC 3986, uppercase hex) over its UTF-8 bytes. "%" is included so the encoding is self-inverse.
Percent-encoding happens at canonicalization time. The stored value stays the human's original bytes.
The hash is "sha256:" followed by 64 lowercase hex characters.

cases.note: Ordinary numeric bounds. Keys follow the profile keyOrder, not alphabetical order.

A value of 20.0 must serialize as "20", not "20.0" — the shortest round-trippable form. An implementation whose number formatter prints a trailing ".0" produces a different hash for the same authorized limit.
A non-integral value keeps its shortest form.

A profile with an empty scope schema. The canonical string is "" and its hash is the well-known sha256 of the empty string. It MUST still be present in the mandate payload — a missing scope_hash is a malformed mandate, not "no scope".

The escape rules, all in one value: "=" (0x3D) and "%" (0x25) are percent-encoded so the encoding is self-inverse, and every byte outside printable ASCII 0x20-0x7E is encoded as its UTF-8 bytes. Here the em-dash U+2014 becomes %E2%80%94. Percent-encoding happens at canonicalization time; the stored value remains the human's original bytes.
A subset scope field carries the canonical joined form the Gatekeeper compares against.

Optional keys the human did not set are OMITTED — no record is emitted. read_max_age_days and read_daily_max are in keyOrder and absent from values. An implementation that renders a placeholder (the literal text "undefined", or "key=") commits the hash to a value the human never entered.
A key PRESENT with an empty string renders as "key=" — a different commitment from absence. Here allowed_recipients was set to "" and allowed_domains to one domain.

must_refuse.note: The value carries a raw LF. This is a refusal, not an encoding case: a hash computed over silently-stripped input does not represent what the human authorized.
